intro:
You settle the parameters of a new service from change-board decisions, a design doc, a readme, a wiki and chat.

Initial specification:
- [e001] Precedence rule: when sources disagree, the order of authority is change-board > design-doc > readme > wiki > chat. Inside one source, the higher version wins.
- [e002] The design-doc document DD-1 (version 1) states that the password hash algorithm is `scrypt`.
- [e003] According to design-doc DD-1 version 1, the data residency region is `uk-zone`.
- [e004] The design-doc document DD-1 (version 1) states that the data retention in days is `180`.
- [e005] According to design-doc DD-1 version 1, the default currency is `SEK`.
- [e006] According to design-doc DD-1 version 1, the strict validation mode is `OFF`.
- [e007] The design-doc document DD-1 (version 1) states that the session timeout in minutes is `30`.
- [e008] The design-doc document DD-1 (version 1) states that the export file format is `parquet`.
- [e009] The design-doc document DD-1 (version 1) states that the API rate limit per minute is `600`.
- [e010] The design-doc document DD-1 (version 1) states that the maximum payload size in KB is `1024`.
- [e011] The readme document README-137 (version 2) states that the minimum TLS version is `tls-1.1`.

Sources, from highest to lowest authority: change-board, design-doc, readme, wiki, chat. When two sources disagree, the higher one decides.
Inside one source, a higher version number overrides a lower one. A withdrawn document no longer counts at all.
Every event has a label of the form [eNNN] with a three-digit number. A higher number is later in time. A later event can change or cancel an earlier one.
Some material quotes old pages or copies for history. A quote of that kind is not a new statement.

Keep track of every change. Reply with a short acknowledgement when you have read everything.
